newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-FRANCE'S TAPIE ORDERED BACK TO COURT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FRANCE'S TAPIE ORDERED BACK TO COURT.

text.p: A French judge on Tuesday ordered fallen tycoon Bernard Tapie to stand trial over suspected irregularities in the finances of Marseille soccer club, the team he took to the European cup title in 1993.
Tapie, his former deputy Jean-Pierre Bernes, former soccer international Michel Hidalgo and 17 others will stand trial on suspicion they misused corporate funds and falsified documents.

The target of a blizzard of legal actions over his now destroyed business empire, the former Marseille chairman has already been sentenced to jail terms of eight and six months for tax fraud and rigging a soccer match. He is appealing both cases in the supreme court.
A former cabinet minister, Tapie was stripped of his seat in the National Assembly after he was declared bankrupt and ineligible for public office.
But he is still a member of the European Parliament, which has deferred a decision to strip him of his seat until the appeals procedure had run its full course.
